items.title: Show HN: StenifyAI – AI-generated meeting minutes based on meeting type
items.raw_excerpt: We built StenifyAI, a lightweight tool that generates structured meeting minutes from real conversations. It works for both in-person and online meetings, and the output format changes depending on the type of meeting (product sync, client call, brainstorming, lecture, etc.). We started this during a 24-hour Cursor hackathon and spent the past month tightening the UX and accuracy. We built it because most AI summarisation tools give generic notes that miss decisions or ownership. Our own meetings often ended with unclear action items. Instead of a one-size-fits-all summary, we built templates tuned for specific meeting formats. Technical overview: • System audio capture for online calls • Mic capture for in-person meetings • Prompt-layer guided summaries based on meeting type • Timestamp-b

excerpt_i18n.en:
Baidu's Wenku and Netdisk have officially expanded overseas. At this year's Baidu World Conference, in addition to emphasizing "internalized AI," Baidu announced the latest progress in the global rollout of several flagship products. Baidu Wenku and Netdisk are at the forefront, serving as the "vanguard" for Baidu's exploration of the global AI market.

Although large foundational models are developing rapidly and impressively worldwide, creating an "illusion" that AI is all-powerful, the reality is different. Overseas companies, employees, and students alike are constrained by the unhealthy "inverted pyramid" structure in the AI industry—more specific and personalized usage scenarios and needs remain largely unmet.

In China, Baidu Wenku, as a one-stop AI content acquisition and creation platform covering work, study, entertainment, and daily life, has surpassed 90 million monthly active users, firmly leading its field. However, overseas, products with comprehensive multimodal capabilities are rare—integrating understanding, generation, and editing of text, images, audio, and video across the entire process, along with task decomposition, path planning, and workflow orchestration. In short, overseas AI products are often vertical and fragmented, making all-in-one solutions like Baidu Wenku hard to find.

Particularly in regions such as the Middle East, Southeast Asia, and South America, the adoption of AI capabilities remains at levels seen years ago, leaving a significant market gap.

Baidu Netdisk faces similar opportunities. Many overseas Chinese look to it to stay connected with family and friends back home, share life experiences, use AI to preserve shared memories, and build an "online home" that bridges physical distances.

Top AI minds converged to discuss AI's next decade. Turing Award laureate, academician of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and dean of Tsinghua University's Institute for Interdisciplinary Information Sciences and School of Artificial Intelligence, Yao Qizhi, delivered a keynote speech titled "Future Prospects of Artificial Intelligence." He stated that large AI models are revolutionizing various industries, with the medium to long-term goal being the advancement toward AGI to empower science, while ensuring AI is safe, controllable, and reliable. Its prospects are vast and its impact profound, necessitating continuous innovation and breakthroughs. China has no shortage of application talent and scenarios; the most critical need is to cultivate more cutting-edge innovative talent.

Representing the younger pioneering forces, Wang Xingxing, founder and CEO of Unitree Robotics, shared his deeply held dreams and aspirations in a speech titled "Our Next Decade." He emphasized that the next decade will be one of "growth and blossoming"—a period where robots evolve from "capable of tasks" to "skilled at tasks," transitioning from "industry tools" to "life partners."

In recent years, the AI industry has moved at an almost surreal pace. Models have repeatedly pushed boundaries, product iterations race against time, and discussions have shifted from "reasoning costs" to "emergent intelligence" and "AGI timelines," with sentiments swinging between optimism and anxiety. Amid such intense technological cycles, few pause to consider a more fundamental question: What kind of intelligence are we truly pursuing? Beyond language, are there abilities yet to be fully understood?

A week ago, Li Fei-Fei reignited this debate with a lengthy article on world models, which avoided hype about revolution or offering easy futures. Its weight lay in highlighting the tough challenges current technology often sidesteps: spatial understanding, physical reasoning, embodied behavior, and real-world uncertainties—long-avoided issues laid out one by one, sparking intense discussions on world models within the AI community.

A week later, in a recent interview, Li Fei-Fei revisited the unresolved aspects of that article, breaking down the questions she had pondered repeatedly but couldn't fully expand on in writing. She provided more detailed explanations on the structural shortcomings of language models in world understanding, the foundational role of 3D space in intelligence formation, and the unavoidable real-world constraints behind the long stagnation in robotics.

As these fragmented clues were reorganized, the interview itself served as a continuation and completion of the original article, offering a clearer view of the technical directions she genuinely focuses on and the logic behind them.

Globally, 88% of enterprises have adopted AI technologies, yet only 39% have achieved significant financial returns. This "input-output ratio" gap in AI highlights the core challenge of its industrial implementation. Intelligent agents are seen as the key wave to solve this problem, but how can they move beyond being labeled as "toys" or "concepts" to deeply integrate into industries and become productive forces that reduce costs and increase efficiency? On November 13, at the Baidu World 2025 Intelligent Agent Forum, Baidu Intelligent Cloud, in collaboration with industry and technology experts from Intel, the Key Laboratory of Big Data and AI Applications Innovation for Emergency Management, and the Digital Engineering Research Institute of China Energy Engineering Group Guangdong Institute, provided the answer: an outstanding intelligent agent must be built on a solid infrastructure. A robust Agent Infra serves as the core engine that transforms agents from "potential" into "productivity."

Building the Productivity Engine: Baidu Qianfan Agent Infra Lays the "Foundation"

The implementation of enterprise-level agents is far from a simple "large model + prompts." Yin Dawei, General Manager of Baidu Intelligent Cloud's Platform Product Division, emphasized at the forum that intelligent agent technology has evolved over the past three years from chatbots to multimodal enterprise capabilities, requiring a unified, efficient, and scalable infrastructure to support increasingly complex development and operations. To address this, Baidu Intelligent Cloud has built a comprehensive Agent Infra centered around Baidu Qianfan, integrating agent development services, tool services, model services, and data services.
excerpt_i18n.es: El 88 % de las empresas a nivel mundial ya han implementado tecnologías de IA, pero solo el 39 % ha logrado un retorno financiero significativo. Esta brecha en la relación "inversión-resultado" de la IA revela el núcleo del desafío en su aplicación industrial. Los agentes inteligentes se consideran la clave para superar este obstáculo, pero ¿cómo pueden dejar de ser meros "juguetes" o "conceptos" y convertirse en verdaderas herramientas de productividad que reduzcan costes y mejoren la eficiencia en la industria? El 13 de noviembre, en el Foro de Agentes Inteligentes de Baidu World 2025, Baidu Intelligent Cloud, junto con Intel, el Laboratorio Clave de Innovación en Aplicaciones de Big Data e IA del Ministerio de Gestión de Emergencias, y el Instituto de Ingeniería Digital del Grupo de Construcción Energética de China en Guangdong, entre otros expertos industriales y técnicos, ofrecieron la respuesta: excelencia.

excerpt_i18n.en:
At Europe's largest SME summit CoCreate, it was learned that Alibaba International Station will launch AI Mode for global business buyers, using AI Agents to fully automate cross-border e-commerce procurement processes for SMEs worldwide. Industry analysis suggests Alibaba is transforming foreign trade procurement into the next major AI gateway, offering new benefits for domestic and international trade firms.

AI Mode features three key aspects: 1) deeper industry understanding to help buyers make faster, more accurate decisions; 2) AI Agent capabilities to handle tedious tasks with one click, eliminating repetitive work; 3) multimodal mining of hidden supply chain information for more comprehensive consideration and precise matching. This will significantly lower global trade barriers and attract more targeted overseas buyers.

Alibaba International Station President Zhang Kuo stated that AI is profoundly reshaping e-commerce, particularly in B2B global trade scenarios with longer decision chains and higher per-order values, where AI's impact is especially significant.
excerpt_i18n.es: Según se supo en la cumbre CoCreate, el mayor encuentro de pymes de Europa, Alibaba International lanzará AI Mode para compradores empresariales globales, utilizando agentes de IA para automatizar completamente los procesos de compra en el comercio transfronterizo. Los análisis del sector indican que Alibaba está transformando la adquisición de productos de comercio exterior en la próxima gran puerta de entrada de IA, lo que traerá nuevos beneficios a las empresas de comercio exterior nacionales. AI Mode presenta tres características principales: 1) Mayor comprensión del sector, permitiendo a los compradores tomar decisiones más rápidas y precisas; 2) Capacidad de realizar tareas tediosas de un solo clic con agentes de IA, eliminando el trabajo repetitivo; 3) Capacidad multimodal para descubrir oportunidades ocultas.
